questions.solution:

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** They said to him, “Do not jump into the pond today.”

• The imperative verb "Do not jump" changes to "not to jump."
 
• The phrase "into the pond today" changes to "into the pond that day" to maintain the same timeframe.
 
• "Said to" changes to "told."
 
 
 
• **Correct Format:** The direct speech command is turned into a reported command in indirect speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

questions.question:

Miranda said to her teacher, "I was sick for a day."

options.text: Miranda told her teacher that she has been sick for a day.
Miranda told her teacher that she is sick for a day.
Miranda told her teacher that she was sick for a day.
Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day'.**

__
 
• The** correct indirect form **of the sentence *"Miranda said to her teacher, 'I was sick for a day.'*" **is** *"Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day."*
 
• When converting direct speech into indirect speech, the tense of the verbs usually shifts back (this is known as "backshifting").
 
• In this case, the** past simple tense** "was" **changes to **the past perfect tense "had been."
 
• This shift accurately conveys the timing of the events in the indirect speech.

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: *'Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **"Miranda told her teacher that she has been sick for a day." **- This is incorrect because the present perfect "has been" doesn't accurately convey the timing of past events in indirect speech.
 
• **"Miranda told her teacher that she is sick for a day."** - This is incorrect because the present tense "is" doesn't accurately represent the past events conveyed in the original direct speech.
 
• **"Miranda told her teacher that she was sick for a day." **- Although it might seem correct in some contexts, in proper English grammar, while changing from direct to indirect speech, the tense usually shifts back. Therefore, "was" should become "had been."
